policy_note: Controlled vocabularies for the local extraction stage. Additions are new registry versions, never ad-hoc strings. v1 is retained verbatim for replay of anything extracted under it.

why_v2.defect: v1 asked GLiNER for 25 labels, most of which are ONTOLOGICAL CATEGORIES rather than entity types: QUALITY, BEHAVIOR, STATE, PROCESS, GOAL, OUTCOME, CONDITION, METRIC, SIGNAL, BASELINE, POPULATION, INTERVENTION, GROUP, AGENT. A zero-shot NER model asked for QUALITY correctly returns 'good' and 'painful'; asked for BEHAVIOR it returns 'habits', 'desires', 'addicted'. That is the model answering the question it was asked. GLiNER's documented weakness is common-noun misclassification, and an abstract label set maximises it.
why_v2.note_on_person: PERSON measured 0.11 but is NOT dropped. It scored low only because it catches pronouns and role nouns, and it is the right label for a real name. That is a filtering problem, handled by entity_quality.py, not a vocabulary problem.
why_v2.ontology_alignment: v1 labels were 100% outside config/ontology.yaml, so the allowed_pairs gate could only ever pass relations whose types it could not check. v2 labels map 1:1 onto ontology entity_types, making that gate load-bearing instead of decorative.

measured_ab.harness: 80 real corpus chunks, GLiNER medium-v2.1, judged by survival through the deterministic entity quality gate
measured_ab.verdict: v2 yields 22% MORE graph-eligible entities from 21% FEWER raw mentions. Strictly better on both precision and useful yield, and cheaper downstream.
measured_ab.rejected_alternative: Natural-language descriptive labels ('named person', 'company or institution') were tested and are WORSE: they raised the pronoun rate from 13.4% to 21.4% by concentrating output into a 'named person' bucket that attracts pronouns. Simple lowercase type nouns won.

threshold_note: 0.45 maximises graph-eligible yield (4.00/chunk). 0.55 raises gate survival to 64.2% at 3.81/chunk and cuts downstream work ~20%; choose it if extraction cost dominates. Below 0.35 the common-noun failure mode returns.
dropped_rationale: Every one is an ontological category rather than an entity type, has no ontology.yaml equivalent, and measured at or near zero graph-worthiness. RESOURCE (0.33) is folded into 'artifact'; TIME_PATTERN is dropped because dates are weak graph nodes and temporal capture already has its own contract (temporal_captures).
predicate_types_note: Retained verbatim from v1 for contract compatibility. UNUSED by the current lane: GLiREL is retired and relations are produced by the frame-licensed spaCy extractor against config/predicate_synonyms.yaml. Kept so v1-era artifacts remain replayable.
